seoTitle: Chinese New Year 2027 Factory Closures: Order Deadlines and Calculator
description: Chinese New Year 2027 is on 6 February, but Chinese factories wind down from late January. Key dates, a last-order-date calculator and an AI checklist to get stock shipped before the shutdown.
keywords: when to order before chinese new year
title: Chinese New Year 2027: when to place orders before Chinese factories close
lede: The holiday is on 6 February 2027, but production stops one to two weeks earlier and restarts slowly. If your Q1 stock is made in China, the real deadline is in December. Here are the dates, a calculator and a way to get every supplier's schedule in writing tonight.
intro: Chinese New Year (Spring Festival) 2027 falls on Saturday, 6 February. New Year's Eve is 5 February, and the statutory public holidays in mainland China run from 5 to 8 February. With weekends and adjusted working days, the official break is usually around 8-9 days.

Factories close much longer than that. Workers travel home in the last week of January, many lines stop around 25-27 January and full capacity often only returns in March. That is why the date that matters for you is not 6 February but your supplier's last pickup day.

timeline.title: Get schedules in writing
timeline.body: Ask every supplier for four dates: last order day, last production day, last pickup day and the day production fully restarts.

timeline.title: Lock specs and prices
timeline.body: Approve samples, artwork and packaging now. Any change in January restarts production and misses the window.

timeline.title: Place orders and pay deposits
timeline.body: Order 6-10 weeks of extra stock to cover the closure and the slow restart. Book freight space at the same time.

timeline.title: Inspect before it leaves
timeline.body: Schedule a pre-shipment inspection. Rushed end-of-year production is where quality problems usually appear.

timeline.title: Re-check quality and prices
timeline.body: Many workers change jobs after the festival. Inspect the first post-holiday batch and recheck quotes and lead times.

risks: Planning against 6 February instead of the supplier's last pickup day.
Changing packaging or specs in January, which restarts production.
Ordering only for February: the slow restart often stretches lead times into March.
Skipping inspection on rushed end-of-year runs and on the first post-holiday batch.
Booking freight late: space and rates tighten in the weeks before the holiday.

faq.a: Saturday, 6 February 2027. New Year's Eve is 5 February, and mainland China's statutory holidays are 5-8 February. The final days off are set by the State Council notice.

faq.q: When do Chinese factories close for Chinese New Year 2027?
faq.a: It depends on the factory. Many stop production around 25-27 January 2027 and restart around the Lantern Festival on 20 February, with full capacity often only in March.

faq.q: What is the last date to order before Chinese New Year 2027?
faq.a: For goods that must ship before the break, most suppliers recommend placing orders by mid-December 2026. Use the calculator above with your supplier's real pickup date and production time.

faq.q: How much extra stock should I order?
faq.a: A common rule is 6-10 weeks of extra stock: the closure itself plus the slow restart and transit. Fast-moving products may need more.

faq.q: Can AI help with Chinese New Year planning?
faq.a: Yes. An AI sourcing agent such as Accio can request holiday schedules from suppliers, compare them in one table, find backup suppliers and recalculate landed cost.
